scope: Research of Rust protocol 2635 and official EAC/EOS session requirements. No authenticated Rust player connection has been established.

provenance.source: Steam anonymous dedicated-server subscription, app 258550, public branch, Windows

facts.finding: After transport admission, the server sends RequestUserInformation.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: The application message header is the enum value plus 140; it is not a raw UDP packet identifier.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: The server validates the application connection marker and protocol, and reads Steam and anti-cheat identity data.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: The authentication coroutine runs Steam, EAC and additional server admission checks before queue admission.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: The Steam platform session is started using the supplied Steam ID and token.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: EAC registration and authentication progress are separate from the Steam session.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: Approval includes world data and the selected network encryption level.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: ClientReady is a Protobuf message and advances a welcoming connection into the connected state.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: PlayerTick is deserialized with ProtoDelta using the previous received tick.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: Full PlayerTick includes input, position, model state, identifiers and time delta.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: ClientReady has clientInfo, globalNetworking and party fields.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: The common EOS login wrapper selects ExternalCredentialType.SteamAppTicket (1). This is not proof of a successful client login.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: EOS identity token issuance uses the Connect interface and a ProductUserId.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: The protected server initializes an EOS AntiCheatServer session and sets its registration timeout to 20 seconds.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: The protected path registers a client handle and the claimed ProductUserId with the EOS AntiCheatServer interface.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: Local and remote authentication callbacks are distinct; remote completion starts identity-token verification.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: When identity-token verification is enforced, failed verification or a mismatch between AccountId and the Steam user ID results in rejection.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: This helper checks for RemoteAuthComplete (2). It is not the only admission gate; strict-auth configuration affects earlier progression.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: EAC payloads are passed to the official ReceiveMessageFromClient interface.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: A server network-protection path uses EOS ProtectMessage; actual target encryption configuration was not read.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: The corresponding network-protection path uses EOS UnprotectMessage.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: The EAC network-active state is adjusted for loading.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: The EAC network-active state is adjusted when loading finishes.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

facts.finding: Rust includes a RakNet client wrapper that calls the native transport; the complete native handshake was not reconstructed.
facts.evidenceKind: static analysis, not successful player login

excludedConclusions: A2S secure/VAC flags do not establish the EAC enforcement settings.
Matching protocol 2635 does not establish identical client/server build IDs or byte-for-byte identity with the target.
SDK availability and valid EOS identity alone do not establish a valid protected EAC client session.
The listed message and schema facts are partial and do not constitute a complete playable Rust client.
